Hyman's figures include 6,155 Class B shares held by her spouse and 10,521 RSUs vesting within 60 days.

notes: Fiscal year 2024 ended January 31, 2025 (Rent the Runway's own label; matches data.js fy 'Jan 2025'). A later proxy (September 2025, for a special meeting) was not used. OWNERSHIP BASIS: the proxy's unlabeled 'Total' column is used as the economic percentage. For Hyman (3.6%) and the officer group (8.5%) it matches holdings over all Class A and Class B shares. For the Class A-only holders it repeats the Class A percentage (Bain 10.6%), which is slightly above their share of both classes combined. The figures are recorded as printed and not recomputed. pctVoting is null because no voting-power percentage is stated. The holder filings are old (Bain's 13G is from February 2022), so asOf is null. CASH: no dividends have ever been paid. Financing cash flows were only $2.0 million of short-term financing proceeds and $(2.3) million of other financing payments, with no repurchase line, so buybacks are 0. STOCK COMP: $9.7 million, shown as 0.01 billion after rounding. GEOGRAPHY is null: the 10-K reports no geographic revenue split and says 'We do not currently offer our products and services internationally', so all revenue ($306.2 million) is U.S.

paidout.notes: Judgement call: purchases of rental product (garments bought from designers, 49.2m) are counted as capex. PAIDOUT.md excludes lease fleets, but the pilot's reason (captive-finance assets bought largely from the group itself) does not fit: these are payments to outside suppliers and are RTR's main purchase. Excluding them gives paidOut 0.2977bn. Known bias: revenue includes 28.1m of proceeds from rental product sold that the company classifies in investing, not operating, so paidOut is overstated by up to 28.1m.
